question: MKUltra: what did the June 30, 2026 hearing establish, and what is still open?
answer: On June 30, 2026 the House Oversight Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets (chair Rep. Anna Paulina Luna) heard Stephen Kinzer (book: Poisoner in Chief), Tom O'Neill (book: Chaos), Dr. Elizabeth Ginexi (former NIH) on MKUltra. It is a declassification and oversight hearing, not a prosecution, and made no legal finding. The chair committed on the record to contact the German government about Camp King and Villa Schuster. All 5 follow-ups have no recorded status since June 30, 2026, and only 1 of 5 cited sources is primary.

items.title: The Germany thread: Camp King and Villa Schuster
kv: Camp King & Villa Schuster are documented Artichoke sites with active Bundesarchiv FOIA requests naming them (per page).
the specific Adenauer memo and any burial count (per page).

What Luna committed to on the record: "I'm going to reach out to the German government after this to get the ball rolling." The witnesses describe a CIA "black site" chalet in Germany — Villa Schuster, Kronberg, part of the Camp King (Oberursel) complex — where under Operation Artichoke (MKUltra's predecessor) "expendables" were experimented on in the basement, some to death, staffed by recruited Nazi scientists. Victims allegedly buried in former forest plots. An Adenauer memo is said to warn the Chancellor, who declined to investigate.

Why it's the escalation: every other thread is dead men harming Americans on American soil long ago. This one has foreign bodies, a NATO ally that allegedly knew, and a living paper trail in a friendly archive. One confirmed grave and it stops being declassification and becomes unrecovered victims of a US program on allied soil.

The layer: Villa Schuster was built and owned by a Jewish family, seized, then used by the US — with recruited Nazi scientists — to experiment people to death, as a continuation of Nazi work "right down the road." The man who ran the program, Gottlieb, was himself the son of Orthodox Jewish refugees. The Holocaust's machinery, folded forward into the American covert state, in a stolen Jewish house.

items.title: The saved analysis's overall read
items.text: The read: this is not a prosecution — it's a declassification & oversight body. But it is laying the factual record a future reckoning would stand on: naming crimes with elements (obstruction, criminal destruction of federal records, crimes against humanity), re-attaching guilt to the institution, and quietly converting a dead 1950s program into a live question — is there a successor running now?

items.title: Crimes with elements, on the record
items.text: Luna pins named crimes to named men — Helms ordered the 1973 record burn, Gottlieb executed it, the records chief protested in writing and was overruled. "Crimes against humanity" is the one frame that carries no statute of limitations and reclassifies MKUltra from old scandal to unresolved crime.

items.title: Three doors, propped open
items.text: (1) Newly-found boxes — a forgery program housed under MKUltra, being declassified now. (2) The Germany outreach (see below). (3) The redaction fight — un-redacting what we already have, taken straight to the CIA director. Each can pay off later.

items.title: "Is it still happening?"
items.text: Both authors swing present-tense — AI, neuroscience, cyber, "a 21st-century MKUltra." You can't investigate a program that ended in 1973, but you can investigate whether a successor exists. That's the bridge from declassification to active oversight of the agencies now.

items.title: Institution vs. scapegoat
items.text: Kinzer argues Gottlieb was chosen as the disownable outsider so the CIA could blame one man. Re-attaching guilt to the institution is the logical prerequisite for any accountability aimed at the agency itself — because the men are dead, but the institution persists.

items.title: The assassination cluster
items.text: Olson, Ruby (West kept him from talking), MLK's "climate," Manson/Chaos — then Rep. Burchett drags it live: could this "cause someone to take a shot at a president… the Butler shooting… even the Charlie Kirk shooting." Kinzer won't speculate but won't deny the mechanism. A marker that gets cited later.

items.title: The NIH collision
items.text: The majority jams "trust the science / COVID" against "the CIA experimented on you and hid it." Both are one story: an institution the people funded, that lied, and won't answer. Kinzer hands them the spine — conspiracy theories as rational responses to a real "covert sphere." The populist thesis of the whole chronicle, said aloud.
